A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Omni-Mol, with identifiable continuity in architecture, tasks and experiments despite substantial revisions. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular-task evaluations, scaling experiments, ablations, representation analyses and efficiency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 reports original evaluations across 16 tasks, alongside 3D-input experiments, additional ablations, DRD2-scoring experiments and a continual-learning test.

M1.justification: V1's iterative active-learning data-selection algorithm, a central training component in Section 3.3, is absent from v3's proposed procedure. V3 also introduces a 3D variant using Uni-Mol as graph encoder. The adaptive LoRA and shared/routed-expert design remains recognizable under the GAL/MoGE terminology; those renamings alone are not method additions.

E1.justification: V3 removes SCF-energy and complexity prediction while adding IUPAC2SELFIES, text-guided molecule generation and ZINC-based molecule editing, changing coverage from 15 to 16 tasks. Appendix E.2 additionally evaluates ten tasks with 3D molecular inputs, extending the input conditions beyond v1's 2D graph setting.

E2.justification: V3 replaces Vicuna's in-context rows with DeepSeekV3 on forward prediction, retrosynthesis and reagent prediction, and adds DeepSeekV3 comparisons elsewhere. GPT-3.5-turbo disappears from captioning and Alpaca from quantum-property prediction. Appendix E.3 newly compares Omni-Mol with GraphMVP, GraphMVP-G and GraphMVP-C on retained regression tasks.

E3.justification: The reported batch size changes from 32 to 128, and the main Omni-Mol configuration from 1.7B to 2.2B parameters. New experiments introduce 3D conformer preprocessing, constrained and unconstrained editing metrics, clustered DRD2-scoring splits and sequential task training. These materially change evaluation settings; the revised scores are not controlled same-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: V3 adds rank sensitivity, language-backbone, head-tuning and GAL-clipping analyses, DRD2-scorer generalization tests, molecule-editing cases and continual-learning analysis. Unified-training and component ablations use revised tasks and controls. V1's data-selection, functional-group routing and efficiency analyses disappear. The representation-similarity heatmap and earlier reaction/captioning cases are retained, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions specify random seed 0. V1's Figure 11 explicitly averages three efficiency runs; that experiment and its repetition disclosure disappear in v3. V3's checklist asserts that statistical significance was considered, but supplies no corresponding defined error bars, confidence intervals or testing procedure.

E6.justification: Reported Omni-Mol results change substantially: forward exact match changes from 0.718 to 0.73, reagent exact match from 0.257 to 0.23, and average quantum-property MAE from 0.0052 to 0.0044. These accompany different model configurations. V3 adds generation, editing, 3D and new analysis outcomes, while removing SCF, complexity and efficiency results.

T1.justification: V3 removes v1's Section 3.6 solution-space formalization, Theorem 3.1 and its Appendix H proof, including the asserted strict contraction under distinct task solution sets. The mutual-nearest-neighbor similarity equations remain, but no replacement convergence theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from resolving conflict collapse through universal convergence and active data selection to unified molecular understanding and generation through GAL/MoGE. The claimed 40%-data efficiency benefit disappears. V3 claims state-of-the-art performance on 13 of 16 tasks, replacing v1's abstract claim across 15 tasks; representation-convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: V3 explains adaptive tuning through task-dependent intrinsic dimensionality, replacing v1's softmax, gradient-growth and bf16-divergence explanation. The stated applicability limit changes from inability to design molecules to restriction to small molecules. New interpretations address editing strategies and sequential forgetting, while v1's discussion of adverse transfer on regression tasks is removed.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies GAL initialization and clipping bounds, software versions, 576 A100 GPU-hours, 3D preprocessing, DRD2-scorer construction and prompts for added tasks. Named GitHub and Hugging Face access links replace the anonymous link. However, Appendix C.1 adds multi-molecule graph concatenation while retaining the contradictory statement that only the first molecule receives graph encoding.

R1.justification: V3 substantially reframes positioning around one shared model covering four modality mappings, supported by a new capability-comparison table and Appendix I's generalist/specialist distinction. New references connect GAL to intrinsic-dimensionality research and OLoRA, PiSSA and LoRA+, and support molecular editing and Uni-Mol. The active-data-selection antecedent cited in v1 is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten. V1's combined Method section becomes separate Overview, Data Curation and Method sections, with revised terminology and reorganized experiments. Appendices are restructured and a checklist and contents list added, although many task descriptions and prompt templates remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, and formerly separate main-text and appendix results are consolidated into v3's Table 3. The architecture diagram is redesigned and scaling plots become grouped bars. Dataset-distribution, rank-sensitivity and editing displays are added, while conflict, gradient, selection and efficiency displays are removed.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's stated lack of molecule-design capability with actual generation and editing experiments, and adds useful controls and implementation details. However, new reporting conflicts undermine reproducibility and interpretation: Appendix C.1 contradicts itself about graph inputs, and catalyst control rows in Tables 6 and 9 reproduce forward-prediction values rather than Table 3's catalyst results. These material gains and reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
